title: Naval Topic 4 生词 · 英英解释

items.ex: Gains are the good things you get, like money, skills or progress. Most of the gains in life means most of the benefits you get. As a verb, gain means to get or increase something.
exs: I've seen big gains since I started working out.
You'll gain more confidence with practice.

items.ex: On a daily basis means every day or regularly. Basis here means the way or schedule something happens on. We also say on a weekly or a regular basis.
exs: I talk to clients on a daily basis.
Try to practice on a daily basis, even for five minutes.

items.ex: An addict is someone who can't stop doing something. A suffering addict is someone who starts to need the pain itself, as if pain alone proves you're making progress. Chris says people need to avoid becoming one.
exs: Don't become a suffering addict; rest is part of the plan.
He's a bit of a workout addict.

items.ex: Sort of means kind of or a little. People use it to make a statement softer or less exact. It's extremely common in casual American speech.
exs: I'm sort of hungry, but not really.
It's sort of like a lash lift, but different.

items.ex: A proxy is something that stands in for something else. Using suffering as the proxy for progress means treating pain as the sign that you're improving. In business, a proxy can also be a person acting for you.
exs: Hours at work are a bad proxy for how productive you are.
Price isn't always a good proxy for quality.

items.ex: As opposed to compares two things and says you mean the first, not the second. Here it's pain as a sign of progress, as opposed to the real result. It's a clear way to make a contrast.
exs: I prefer mornings, as opposed to late nights.
Focus on quality, as opposed to quantity.

items.ex: Attached means connected or joined to something. Naval says he had attached his well-being to pain, meaning his happiness was linked to suffering. Attached to can also mean emotionally close.
exs: I'm really attached to my old phone.
Don't attach your self-worth to one client's opinion.

items.ex: Well-being means being healthy, comfortable and happy, in body and mind. Naval talks about his overall well-being and satisfaction. It's common in health and work talk.
exs: Sleep is so important for your well-being.
The company cares about employee well-being.

items.ex: Anguish is very strong pain, especially in your mind or heart. Naval says suffering is mostly mental anguish, not physical pain. It's a strong, serious word.
exs: You could see the anguish on his face.
Waiting for the results was pure anguish.

items.ex: The task at hand is the job you need to do right now. At hand means close or right in front of you. People say focus on the task at hand.
exs: Put your phone away and focus on the task at hand.
Let's get back to the task at hand.

items.ex: Effective means it works well and gets the result you want. Naval asks which is more effective: suffering, or seeing it in a different way. Very common at work and in health.
exs: This cleanser is really effective.
What's the most effective way to learn English?

items.ex: To interpret means to decide what something means, or to explain it in your own way. Interpret it in a way that's not suffering means see the same situation differently. It also means translating speech between languages.
exs: How do you interpret her message?
She interprets for Chinese clients at the clinic.

items.ex: A journey is a long trip, and here it means the whole process of reaching a goal. Successful people say the journey was the fun part, meaning the path, not the finish line. Very common in motivational talk.
exs: Learning English is a journey, not a race.
Enjoy the journey.

items.ex: Entertaining means fun and interesting to watch, do or listen to. Naval says the hard path was actually the entertaining part. We use it for people, shows and stories.
exs: The podcast is really entertaining.
He's an entertaining guy to work with.

items.ex: A regret is a feeling of being sorry about something you did or didn't do. It's a common regret means many people feel this way. As a verb: I regret not trying.
exs: My only regret is not starting sooner.
You won't regret it.
